claim: Candidate: a canonical sparse Merkle map fits per-key state; roots must be derived from canonical content rather than arrival order. Source: https://transparency.dev/verifiable-data-structures/

Utreexo is a dynamic hash accumulator, but insertion order affects its structure; direct adoption must preserve CBCL set-invariance or bind an explicit canonical ordering. Sources: https://eprint.iacr.org/2019/611 and https://github.com/utreexo/biptreexo/blob/main/bip-0182.md

Pointproofs and Verkle-style commitments are candidates for batching many state openings; neither proves fold correctness solely through openings. Sources: https://eprint.iacr.org/2020/419 and https://verkle.dev/docs/concepts/math/multipoint

Design inference: a whole-object snapshot can be hash-checked against an endorsed root without per-entry membership proofs. Advanced accumulators may benefit partial loading and selective continuation more than initial whole-object transfer.
